title: Veneto Slips Under Two Euros — And Stays There
dek: Six straight days of easing pump prices have left Veneto's self-service petrol at €1.9953 a litre, just below both the two-euro line and the national average — while its methane quietly runs the other way.
body: Drivers in Veneto paid an average of €1.9953 per litre for self-service Benzina on August 10th, a whisker under the national self-service mark of €1.9981. The gap is wider on diesel: Gasolio self-service came in at €2.0984 regionally against €2.1071 nationally, leaving Veneto 0.87 cents per litre cheaper than the country as a whole. On a single fill that is loose change, but the discount has pointed the same way all week, on both fuels — this is a region sitting a fraction on the right side of average rather than a bargain outlier.

The direction is downward and has been for six consecutive tracked days. Benzina peaked at €2.0099 on August 4th, crossed back under two euros on August 7th, and has eased every reading since; Gasolio came off a €2.1183 peak on the same date to today's figure, 1.99 cents lower. The steps are shrinking, though — between yesterday and today both fuels moved by less than a tenth of a cent, which reads more like a slide finding its floor than a fresh downswing. Methane is the counter-current: €1.6162 per kg regionally against €1.5650 nationally, and up 6.86 cents since July 21st while petrol fell. Underpinning all of it, 1,836 of Veneto's 1,997 registered stations filed a price today — a 91.9% reporting rate against 90.5% nationally, a network still actively repricing in the middle of August.

Detail at this resolution — one region, four fuels, daily moves measured in hundredths of a cent — is only worth anything if it is never stale. Today's national run alone processed 93,091 price rows across 23,958 registered stations, every one of which has to be fetched, joined to the station registry and re-aggregated before the numbers mean a thing. Fuel Dashboard does that unattended each morning: ingest the MIMIT open data, recompute national, regional, provincial, comune and brand-level averages, rotate the spotlight through all twenty regions on a fixed calendar cycle, and republish the live site with nobody opening a file. It was built with Claude Code, and that is the whole argument — a hand-kept spreadsheet is accurate the day you close it, and this one is accurate today.
pull_quote: Six days under two euros — and the daily drop has now shrunk to less than a tenth of a cent.
caption:
Today's Fuel Dashboard spotlight falls on Veneto, which has quietly slipped under a psychological line: self-service petrol at €1.9953 per litre on August 10th, below both the two-euro mark and the national average of €1.9981. Diesel is a touch friendlier still — €2.0984 regionally against €2.1071 nationally.

It is the sixth consecutive day of falling prices in the region, off a peak on August 4th. But the moves are getting smaller: less than a tenth of a cent between yesterday and today, which usually means a slide running out of road rather than a trend building.

The contrarian number is methane. While petrol drifted down, Veneto's Metano climbed 6.86 cents since July 21st to €1.6162 per kg — over 5 cents above the national figure. Two fuels, same region, opposite directions, same three weeks.

One more sign of a live network: 1,836 of Veneto's 1,997 registered stations reported a price this morning, 91.9% against 90.5% nationally.

Fuel Dashboard tracks Italian fuel prices daily from official MIMIT open data — Benzina, Gasolio, GPL and Metano, self and full service, filterable by region, province, comune and brand, with day-by-day history. Have a look: https://adeo-blip.github.io/fuel-price-italy/

Here is the part worth arguing about. Today's run processed 93,091 price rows from 23,958 stations. Maintained by hand in Excel, that is a morning of downloading, pasting, repairing broken joins and re-dragging formulas — and by the time the chart looks right, the data is a day old. I built the pipeline with Claude Code instead: fetch, join, aggregate, regenerate, redeploy, every morning, unattended. AI tooling did not make the spreadsheet faster. It made the spreadsheet unnecessary.

If you are still babysitting a manual reporting file every morning, that is the first workflow to point an AI coding tool at.
